metadata.noteEn: Gilbert Baker’s original 1978 flag carried eight stripes; the six-stripe version became the standard in 1979.
The chevron adds the trans flag colours, brown and black for communities of colour, and black for those living with HIV/AIDS and those lost to it — pointing right to show forward motion.

stripes.meaningEn: Those transitioning, intersex people, and those of neutral or undefined gender

metadata.noteEn: The pattern is symmetrical, so the flag is always correct however it is flown.

stripes.meaningEn: Trans and gender non-conforming gay men
People with many or all genders
Genders that mix male and female

metadata.noteEn: Chosen by community vote on the Asexual Visibility and Education Network in 2010.
The black triangle at the hoist stands for asexuality.

stripes.meaningEn: Yellow and purple — chosen as colours free of gendered associations

metadata.noteEn: The unbroken circle stands for wholeness and the right to bodily autonomy.
DeBlase deliberately assigned no meanings to the stripes or the heart, leaving interpretation to the viewer.
The stripes represent the fur colours of bears around the world, not individual meanings.

metadata.label: Drag competition series
metadata.blurb: Episodic television: the Drag Race franchises alongside independent shows like Dragula, La Más Draga and Drag Den. Each season carries an episode-by-episode placement grid.
metadata.metaTitle: Drag Competition Series: Every Season | Queer Guide
metadata.metaDescription: Every season of the Drag Race franchises and the independent drag competition series, with winners, runners-up and an episode-by-episode placement grid.

metadata.label: Drag king competitions
metadata.blurb: Competitions for drag kings. King of Drag is a television series and sits here rather than with the other series, because filed among the queen franchises it would be one row in thirty-three.
metadata.metaDescription: Drag king competitions: King of Drag and the San Francisco Drag King Contest, which has run since 1994.

metadata.label: Drag pageantry
metadata.blurb: Drag pageantry systems, decided at a single event rather than across a season. Miss Gay America has run since 1973 and Miss Continental since 1980, both older than the television.
metadata.metaTitle: Drag Pageantry: Miss Gay America and Miss Continental | Queer Guide
metadata.metaDescription: Drag pageantry systems: Miss Gay America since 1973 and Miss Continental since 1980, with every titleholder by year.

metadata.label: Transgender pageants
metadata.blurb: Beauty pageants for transgender women, including Miss International Queen, which describes itself as the world’s largest, and Miss T World.
metadata.metaDescription: Transgender beauty pageants: Miss International Queen, Miss T World, Miss Star International and Miss Fabulous Thailand, with every titleholder by year.

metadata.label: Gay titleholder contests
metadata.blurb: Titleholder contests for gay men. Mr Gay World is an international final; Mr Gay Europe describes itself as a competition about LGBTQIA+ themes rather than a pageant.
metadata.metaTitle: Gay Titleholder Contests: Mr Gay World and Mr Gay Europe | Queer Guide
metadata.metaDescription: Gay titleholder contests: Mr Gay World, Mr Gay Europe and Mr. Gay India, with every titleholder by year.

metadata.label: Leather & fetish titles
metadata.blurb: Leather and fetish title contests, both run as multi-day conventions. International Mr. Leather has been held since 1979 and calls itself a convention and competition, not a pageant.
metadata.metaTitle: Leather and Fetish Titles: IML and MIR | Queer Guide
metadata.metaDescription: Leather and fetish title contests: International Mr. Leather since 1979 and Mister International Rubber, with every titleholder by year.
